original_paragraph.Materials and Methods - 4.5. GLP-1R affi: The GLP-1 receptor affinity assay was performed in our previous publication16. Compounds 0-VI, and semaglutide were diluted in running buffer from 10 μmol/L to 78.1 nmol/L twice (the running buffer consisted of 100 mL of 10 × PBS, 895 mL of water and 5 mL of P20, and was prepared and used immediately). The collected data were analysed using BioEvaluation Software 2.0. The Langmuir 1:1 model was used to analyse the data, and the binding rate constant (ka), dissociation rate constant (kd), and equilibrium constant (Kd) were calculated.
original_paragraph.Figure 3 caption: Fig. 3. GLP-1R binding activity of a) compounds 0, b) compounds I, c) compounds II, d) compounds III, e) compounds IV, f) compounds V, g) compounds VI, h) semaglutide and i) liraglutide. GLP-1 analogs were applied in PBS-P20 to a carboxydextran-coated sensorchip charged with ~3000 RU of human GLP-1R using a Biacore T200 instrument. The signals for the different GLP-1 analogs concentrations are depicted as colored lines whereas curve fits according to a 1:1 Langmuir model are shown in gray. The resulting affinity parameters for GLP-1 analogs are listed in Table 3.
original_paragraph.Figure 3 sensorgram data: Figure 3 (a-i) shows sensorgrams for GLP-1R binding. The x-axis (Time) ranges from -100 to 350 seconds. The y-axis (Response) is in RU (Response Units). The sensorgrams display association (0-180s) and dissociation (180-350s) phases. The different colored lines represent different concentrations of the compound, with the highest concentration typically showing the highest response. The gray lines represent the curve fits according to a 1:1 Langmuir model. The concentration range is from 10 μmol/L to 78.1 nmol/L, as stated in the methods section.
